text.p: Austrian insurer EA-Generali said on Tuesday it had sold its 4.82 voting stake in bank Creditanstalt to Bank Austria, which took control of Creditanstalt in January.

In a statment, EA-Generali also said Italy's Assecurazioni Generali, which controls the majority of EA-Generali's shares, had acquired a further 2.36 percent voting stake in EA-Generali from Creditanstalt, which sells EA-Generali's products over its counters.

The group added Assecurazioni Generali would also take over directly or indirectly the remaining EA-Generali shares currently owned by Creditanstalt. The bank held a total of 9.79 percent of EA-Generali's equity at the end of 1996.
EA-Generali and Creditanstalt had "made a decision to untangle their cross-holdings step by step," EA-Generali said in a statement.
It added the sales would be priced according to a long-term average of the shares' prices on the Vienna stock exchange. It gave no further details.

Their two joint units, CA-Generali Versicherungs AG and CA-EA Investment Ges.m.b.H, would undergo a valuation. Creditanstalt would eventually take over CA-Generali, while EA-Generali would take on CA-EA Investment.
Bank Austria currently cooperates with Vienna insurer Wiener Staedtische.

The future of the cooperation between EA-Generali and Creditanstalt had been unclear since Bank Austria merged with Creditanstalt earlier this year in a deal valued at some 17 billion schillings. -- Vienna newsroom, +431 53112 274
